source.title: Understanding Nonlinear Implicit Bias via Region Counts in Input Space
source.authors: Jingwei Li; Jing Xu; Zifan Wang; Hui-Shuai Zhang; Jing-Zhao Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no obvious truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own training results under varied learning rates, batch sizes, and data augmentation, measuring decision-region counts on trained networks; this bears directly on V1's claim about training recipes and trained models, but it does not measure training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper trains image classifiers and reports region counts and generalization-gap correlations. Its CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet experiments do not report the near-zero training classification error, corrupted/random-label memorization, or stalling outcomes named in V1. Rows record only reported region-count outcomes. The cited claims about larger learning rates and smaller batches improving generalization are prior work, not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study measures decision-region counts and generalization, not the outcomes in V1–V6. Its theoretical result explicitly assumes the edge-of-stability behavior related to V5 (Assumption 6.2) to derive a region-count bound; it does not test that behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors report strong region-count/generalization-gap correlations and smaller region counts with larger learning rates or smaller batches. Their two-layer ReLU theory gives a learning-rate-dependent upper bound conditional on an edge-of-stability assumption; it does not establish that assumption or prove actual region counts decrease monotonically with learning rate.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains classifiers and measures decision-region counts and their correlation with generalization gap; it does not test training classification error as the claim versions specify.
record.method_sensitivity: Region-count/generalization-gap correlations vary by dataset and architecture; the authors also report variation across optimizer, counting dimension, hyperplane generation, learning rate, batch size, weight decay, and augmentation. Smaller batch sizes and larger learning rates are stated to tend to reduce region counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Decision-region counts correlate strongly with generalization gaps across architectures, datasets, optimizers, and counting methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Region counts estimated on sampled input subspaces predict generalization gaps across the tested image classifiers and training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger learning rates and smaller batches tend to reduce region counts (Section 6.1, Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate and batch size influence the geometric complexity of learned decision boundaries.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 6.3 bounds average region count by O(N/(r²η)) for a two-layer ReLU network, conditional on data assumptions and assumed edge-of-stability scaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, the region-count upper bound decreases with learning rate.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The study reports region counts and generalization-gap correlations rather than training classification error, so it cannot establish the central outcome in V1. Many main correlations are reported as values without uncertainty estimates. The paper acknowledges that the theory for the learning-rate effect uses a simplified two-layer ReLU setting and leaves analysis for more general settings open. Hyperparameter combinations use three random seeds and report averages; the region count is approximated on sampled low-dimensional subspaces.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 2's separate counting-dimension correlations were not extracted as additional rows because they report a different counting method for each network and dataset, exceeding the 60-row cap if fully enumerated; only the dataset correlations were retained. Optimizer-specific and hyperplane-generation correlations for networks other than ResNet18 in Appendix C Tables 6–7 were also left out for the same cap; the tables provide these results.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, random-label fitting, and dependence on capacity, early stopping, or regularization are not tested. Generalization-gap correlations do not identify training-error endpoints.
No teacher-student width sweep or measurement of spurious-local-minimum frequency.
No comparison of training error across plain-network depths and identity-shortcut counterparts.
No initialization comparison measuring learning speed, signal propagation, or trainable depth.
No measurements of initial stability limits, loss recovery, curvature trajectories, threshold hovering with falling loss, or threshold-relative divergence. Edge-of-stability scaling is assumed.
No batch-normalization ablation or Fixup comparison measuring training speed, stability, or learning-rate tolerance.

record.verdict_notes: Correct V1 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. No verdict-bearing results are missing. Figure 5's trends are not measured by R1's correlation, so excerpts E4–E5 should not use R1 as their result row; E5's version identifier R1 is invalid.

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies training hyperparameters and reports region counts/generalization gaps, but does not report training classification error, label corruption, random-label fitting, model-size comparisons, or early stopping outcomes.
No two-layer teacher-student spurious-minima experiment or width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or normalization ablation addressing training error.
No initialization comparison or depth/trainability study.
No learning-rate-above-stability loss trajectory or divergence experiment.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization-free Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained for 200 epochs using SGD with cosine learning rate schedule on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Measured average region count across hyperparameter setups and its correlation with generalization gap.

conditions.value: 3 random seeds per hyperparameter; average metrics

rows.measure: Correlation between region count and generalization gap across setups
rows.note: Aggregate correlation across varied training setups; not a measure of training classification error.
rows.check: The correlation does not establish any version's optimization outcome. R10 repeats this SGD correlation.
